item.mechanism: Elements with lower melting points and lower densities exhibit negative molar ratio deviations because they melt first, spread over a larger surface area, absorb more energy, and evaporate earlier during the rapid SLM heating cycle.
item.system: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy fabricated via Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.operating_conditions: SLM process with linear energy density up to 2.83 J/mm, argon atmosphere (<20 ppm oxygen), rapid heating and cooling cycles
item.supporting_observation: Nb and Mo showed negative deviations of -3.5 at% and -0.16 at% respectively, while Ta and W were closer to nominal; Mo and Nb have lower melting points and densities than Ta and W.
item.scope_limits: The deviation is limited to no more than 5%; the text states this deviation does not influence the phase or microstructure of the HEA.
item.alternatives_considered: Particle size and laser absorption rate also influence deviation; for example, Mo has higher absorption but larger particle size which slows melting and reduces mass loss compared to Nb.
quotes: powders with lower melting point are fused first and the liquid spreads on a larger surface area and absorbs more energy than the solid powders.
the lower-density liquid on the surface is exposed to the laser and receives more energy.
these elements with lower melting points arrive at the boiling point earlier and evaporate more during the SLM process, leading to the negative composition deviation.

item.mechanism: Rapid solidification conditions in SLM (high temperature gradient and cooling rate) limit the growth time of grain nuclei, resulting in extremely fine grains and slender dendritic branches with reduced arm spacing.
item.system: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy fabricated via Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.operating_conditions: SLM process with high density of energy inputs and high cooling rates; rapid solidification
item.supporting_observation: Average grain size is 13.4 μm and primary dendrite arm spacing is 6.59 μm, significantly smaller than the 200 μm grain size and 20–30 μm arm spacing of as-cast samples.
item.scope_limits: The text notes that while this mechanism improves properties, further study of mechanical properties is still necessary.
item.alternatives_considered: Traditional casting processes result in much larger grains and dendrite arm spacings due to slower cooling rates.
quotes: under the rapid solidification condition of the laser processing, the grains and dendrites as a sub-structure grew and developed with an extremely high temperature gradient and cooling rate.
when the grain nuclei formed, their growth-driving force was large but the growth-time was limited.
Thus, the dendritic branches were slender in shape, and the dendrite arm spacing was far less than that in other solidification processes such as casting.

item.mechanism: Grain refinement achieved through the rapid cooling of SLM significantly increases the microhardness of the alloy by impeding dislocation motion, consistent with the Hall–Petch law.
item.system: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy fabricated via Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.operating_conditions: SLM process resulting in fine grains (13.4 μm) compared to arc-melted samples (implied larger grains)
item.supporting_observation: SLM-fabricated sample hardness is 826 Hv, compared to 446 Hv for arc-melted samples and 310–437 Hv for superalloys.
item.scope_limits: The text states that the as-cast NbMoTaW HEA is brittle with plastic strain ɛp = 0.2%, implying the mechanism improves hardness but ductility remains a concern requiring further study.
item.alternatives_considered: Arc melting produces a softer alloy (446 Hv) due to coarser microstructure; pure elements are also softer (max 410 Hv).
quotes: Therefore, the plasticity, fatigue strength, and creep rate of the polycrystal BCC metal are improved when the grain size decreases.

item.mechanism: Composition segregation creates local corrosion couples that increase the alloy's thermodynamic tendency to corrode (more negative potential), but the presence of easy passivation metals (Nb, Mo, Ta) results in a significantly lower corrosion current density.
item.system: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy fabricated via Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.operating_conditions: Electrochemical testing in 3.5%wt NaCl solution; potentiodynamic polarization from -0.2 V to +0.2 V; high voltage scanning (-1.5 to +2 V)
item.supporting_observation: HEA has a more negative self-corrosion potential (-91.57 mV) than 316L steel (-242.45 mV), but a free-corrosion current two orders of magnitude lower (8.716 × 10⁻¹¹ A vs 8.815 × 10⁻⁹ A).
item.scope_limits: The mechanism relies on the existence of Nb, Mo, and Ta as easy passivation metals; slight segregation makes the alloy more 'active' thermodynamically.
item.alternatives_considered: 316L steel shows strong corrosion with depth up to 1 mm, whereas the HEA only shows crack extension and pitting.
quotes: This is because the existence of a small amount of composition segregation in the alloy as mentioned before, which is readily forming corrosion couples and makes the alloy more 'active.'
However, the free-corrosion current of the HEA is reduced by two orders of magnitude compared with that of the 316 L steel.
the elements Nb, Mo, and Ta contained in the alloy are all the easy passivation metals, which contributes to the excellent corrosion resistance in the 3.5 %wt NaCl solution.

item.mechanism: The mixing of elemental powders improves the overall laser absorption rate of the mixture compared to most individual powders, facilitating the melting process.
item.system: Mixed Nb, Mo, Ta, W elemental powders prior to SLM
item.operating_conditions: Powder mixing in a planetary ball mill; laser absorption measurement in argon atmosphere
item.supporting_observation: The absorption of the mixed powder is higher than that of most powders except Mo powder, suggesting that the mixing process helps to improve the absorption.
item.scope_limits: Mo powder alone has higher absorption than the mixed powder because it can trap laser radiation in its hollow structure with gaps.
item.alternatives_considered: Individual powder absorption rates vary (A_Mo > A_W > A_Nb > A_Ta), but the mixture enhances absorption generally.
quotes: It is notable that the absorption of the mixed powder is higher than that of most powders except for Mo powder, suggesting that the mixing process helps to improve the absorption.
The absorption of the Mo powder is higher than that of the mixed powder, since the Mo powder can trap the laser radiation easily in the hollow structure with gaps.

The order of the absorption rate of laser in the elements powder to the laser is A Mo > A W > A Nb > A Ta , as shown in Figure 2 , and the higher the absorption, the more energy the powder will receive at the same time.

item.mechanism: The SLM process enables the formation of a single BCC solid solution in NbMoTaW, which is difficult to achieve with traditional thermal forming due to the high melting point of the alloy.
item.operating_conditions: SLM with linear energy density up to 2.83 J/mm; high cooling rates
item.supporting_observation: XRD results show only one BCC structure solid solution without another metal phase; the process is effective where casting (max 1800 °C) fails.
item.scope_limits: Traditional thermal forming like investment casting cannot reach the necessary melting temperature (NbMoTaW melting point is higher than 1800 °C).
item.alternatives_considered: Vacuum arc melting requires re-melting four times to achieve homogeneity and cannot form arbitrary shapes.
quotes: The melting point of NbMoTaW is higher than that of most common metal alloys.
For the casting process, the highest melting temperature is only 1800 °C, which is far from enough for the NbMoTaW alloy in this study.
Therefore, it is obvious that the SLM process is an effective method to form NbMoTaW HEA.

item.mechanism: Larger particle size in Mo powder slows down the melting rate despite its high laser absorption, resulting in lower mass loss and composition deviation compared to smaller Nb particles.
item.system: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy components (specifically Mo vs Nb powders)
item.operating_conditions: SLM process with mixed powders of varying sizes (Mo: 94.9 μm, Nb: 21.5 μm)
item.supporting_observation: Mo and Nb have similar melting points, but Mo shows much smaller deviation (-0.16 at%) than Nb (-3.5 at%) due to particle size effects.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism explains the difference between Mo and Nb specifically; it is part of a combined effect with melting point and absorption.
item.alternatives_considered: Melting point and density trends alone would predict similar behavior for Mo and Nb, but particle size creates the divergence.
quotes: Specifically, for Mo powder, although it has a higher laser absorption rate, the bigger powder size slows down the rate of melting, which causes lower mass loss and deviation compared with Nb.
It is obvious that the average particle size and laser absorptivity both have a similar variation trend and a certain degree of causal relationship.
although Mo and Nb have very similar melting points, the composition deviation between them is relatively huge, which is caused by particle size and laser absorption.

item.mechanism: The SLM process allows for the fabrication of complex 3D shapes without tools or molds, overcoming the geometric limitations of traditional arc melting for refractory HEAs.
item.operating_conditions: SLM using FORWEDO LM120 equipment with 500 W fiber laser
item.supporting_observation: The study produced a cuboid sample (10 mm × 10 mm × 0.5 mm) and notes SLM can fabricate parts according to 3D CAD data.
item.scope_limits: The text notes that while arc melting can reach high temperatures, it cannot form arbitrary shapes.
item.alternatives_considered: Vacuum arc melting requires re-melting and flipping, and cannot form arbitrary shapes.
quotes: Compared with conventional manufacturing, SLM has the capability of producing 3D parts of complex shapes without tools and molds.
Thus, SLM has many advantages, particularly in the processing of refractory metal materials.
Besides, although the arc melting can go up to the melting point, this method cannot form an arbitrary shape.
